title: USA defeats France for fifth consecutive Women's World Cup gold, September 13
dek: The USA women's basketball team won the FIBA World Cup gold medal against France on September 13, capturing their fifth consecutive World Cup title. Breanna Stewart was named tournament MVP and leads the medal rounds in both points and rebounds, cementing her status as the face of USA Basketball.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: USA defeats France for fifth consecutive World Cup gold; Breanna Stewart named tournament MVP and is undefeated across NCAA Tournament, World Cup, and Olympics competition.
bottom_line: Stewart will chase a fourth Olympic gold in Los Angeles in 2028. The younger generation, headlined by Clark and Reese, enters professional play as international teammates while managing rivalry in franchise competition, a dynamic that will shape USA Basketball's roster decisions for the next Olympic cycle.
body:
The USA women's basketball team won the FIBA World Cup gold medal against France on September 13, according to Yahoo Sports. The victory marks the team's fifth consecutive World Cup title. Breanna Stewart was named tournament MVP.
Stewart led the team in both points and rebounds in the medal rounds. She has compiled four college titles, four World Cup gold medals, and three EuroLeague titles. She co-founded the Unrivaled 3-by-3 league and holds an Unrivaled championship. Stewart is undefeated in the NCAA Tournament, World Cup, and Olympics competition, per Yahoo Sports.
Stewart began her professional career as a small forward, then started at center for Team USA. By the final game, she played point guard for extended stretches. Coach Kara Lawson stated, "She is USA Basketball. When you think of the last 15 years, it's Stewie, and we're just really lucky to be a part of her era of this group," according to Yahoo Sports. Stewart won her first championship at UConn in 2013. If Commissioner's Cup titles are included, she averages 1.5 team trophies per year.
Caitlin Clark contributed 12 points and three assists in the gold medal game.  Clark was drafted by Indiana and Reese by Chicago, two franchises separated by less than 200 miles with an established rivalry. Both are on title contenders with a real shot of meeting in the first round, according to Yahoo Sports.
A'ja Wilson has won the last two WNBA MVP trophies and two of the last three titles in the league. Sue Bird is the U.S. women's national team's managing director. Potential roster candidates for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics include Olivia Miles, JuJu Watkins, Sarah Strong, Hannah Hidalgo, Veronica Burton, and Cameron Brink. Sarah Strong is a UConn junior forward and three-time gold medalist in 3-by-3 competition at the youth level for Team USA. Strong could switch her national team ahead of senior competition, per Yahoo Sports.
